second_order: calling people together to build a McGill mark
theme_note: These codes hold together because participants recruit people, propose a motif, and open a shared place to start building; what varies is whether they call generally, name candidate images, or provide the first venue.

second_order: sending help and strategy through live links and coordinates
theme_note: Participants keep work moving by announcing need, warning of interference, refreshing an expired invite, and posting current coordinates; the help requested varies from alliance to navigation.

second_order: making Red Chiken the April Fools mascot
theme_note: Across the room own joke, participants praise, spell, draw, role-play and ask for flair around Red Chiken; the forms vary from caps-lock ritual to mock admissions and memeposting, and none of these codes is treated as canvas conduct.

second_order: checking what McGill made and correcting its details
theme_note: Participants ask whether an image is theirs, identify the right work, repair damage, and correct the eye and tufts; what varies is whether the mistake concerns authorship, damage, or the design itself.
regrouped_from: split during grouping review from showing and defending the contribution: these passages correct identity or design rather than mobilize defence

second_order: playing along with McGill April Fools jokes
theme_note: Participants publish mock news or troll posts, test whether they are jokes, and answer with satire, laughter or mockery; the specific joke varies and these codes are explicitly not canvas conduct.

second_order: bargaining over Red Chiken with the Void
theme_note: The two exchanges negotiate damage, coexistence, allegiance and repair with a named canvas faction; positions vary from offering compromise to refusing negotiation and demanding repair.

second_order: showing and defending the McGill contribution
theme_note: Participants display the contribution, promise its survival, identify a rival attack and add the work to a defence list; defence varies between warning about rivals, alleging bots and volunteering protection.
regrouped_from: split during grouping review from checking the picture: these passages mobilize or name defence rather than correct what belongs

second_order: celebrating and recounting the finished canvas
theme_note: After and around closure, participants admire the work, congratulate one another, compare it with other universities and explain how hard it was to maintain; celebration varies from brief cheers to a participant own account of effort.
